```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`validate_vcf()` reports VCF-shape and Beagle-target problems without modifying
the input. `repair_vcf()` applies explicitly chosen transformations and only
publishes a result that passes its output validation.

## A dirty starting point

`inst/extdata/tiny_dirty.vcf` ships nine records with deliberately broken
features: invalid POS, multiallelic ALT, REF == ALT, duplicate IDs,
duplicate `(chrom, pos)`, non-diploid GT, missing IDs, and a `GT:DP`
FORMAT line.

```{r}
library(galick)

dirty <- system.file("extdata", "tiny_dirty.vcf", package = "galick")
cat(readLines(dirty), sep = "\n")
```

## Validate against the Beagle target

```{r}
v <- validate_vcf(dirty, target = "beagle")
v$ok
v$errors$code
```

Issue entries are not counts of affected records. One entry can refer to many
records, and several entries can describe the same record. Inspect the evidence
and choose a repair policy before discarding data.

## Investigate allele dependencies

For `REF=A, ALT=G,-`, allele indices mean `0=A`, `1=G`, and `2=-`. A `2/2`
call depends on the unsupported allele; removing it without handling dependent
calls would leave unresolved genotype indices. This synthetic example uses an
arbitrary numeric field, not a vendor-specific quality model:

```{r}
diagnostic_input <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
writeLines(c(
  "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
  '##FORMAT=<ID=GT,Number=1,Type=String,Description="Genotype">',
  '##FORMAT=<ID=Q,Number=1,Type=Float,Description="Custom metric, arbitrary units">',
  "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\tFORMAT\ts1\ts2",
  "1\t100\tm1\tA\tG,-\t.\tPASS\t.\tGT:Q\t2/2:0.8\t0/0:0.9"
), diagnostic_input)

diagnosis <- validate_vcf(diagnostic_input, target = "beagle", diagnostics = "extended")
print(diagnosis)
evidence <- diagnosis$summary$diagnostics
evidence$issue_groups
evidence$allele_usage
evidence$unsupported_alleles
evidence$genotype_summary
evidence$quality_summary
evidence$quality_comparisons
```

`summary(diagnosis)` adds FORMAT declarations, within-record comparisons,
genotype categories and action assessments. The structured tables remain
available for filtering or export. Numeric profiling uses only unambiguous
scalar numeric declarations from the header; missing, non-finite and nonnumeric
values are counted separately. Comparisons use supported calls at the same
record, and ratios require a positive baseline median. No numeric difference
automatically means a deletion, a missing call, or an inaccurate genotype.

Standard mode reports record impact and allele usage without retaining quality
arrays. Extended mode retains finite values on problem records for exact
quantiles and therefore can use additional memory. Partial scans explicitly
limit all evidence to the scanned prefix and skip full-file coordinate/sort
checks. The parser still reads the entire file even for a partial scan.

## Repair

```{r}
clean <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
result <- repair_vcf(dirty, clean)
result$ok
result$summary$step_summary
```

Each step records its `n_in` / `n_out` / `n_changed`. Steps that did
something also surface as `$warnings`:

```{r}
result$warnings$code
```

## Re-validate

```{r}
validate_vcf(clean, target = "beagle")$ok
```

## Re-write minimal VCF

The output is a *minimal* VCF: `repair_vcf()` keeps only `CHROM`, `POS`,
`ID`, `REF`, `ALT`, and `FORMAT=GT`, regardless of what the input
carried. The `GT:DP` cells in the dirty file get rewritten to GT-only:

```{r}
cat(readLines(clean)[6:10], sep = "\n")
```

## Step selection

By default `repair_vcf()` runs all five steps. You can pick a subset; if
that subset is insufficient to make the output pass
`validate_vcf(target = "beagle")`, the function returns
`repair_vcf_remaining_*` errors and writes nothing.

```{r}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
result <- repair_vcf(dirty, out, steps = c("drop_invalid_records"))
result$ok
result$errors$code
file.exists(out)
```

## Chromosome-style normalization

Pass `chrom_style = "numeric"` (or `"chr_prefixed"`) to rewrite labels
in the output and use the normalized form for duplicate detection. This
catches `chr1` + `1` collisions that `as_is` would miss.
